text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The manager of Commercial Bank of Malawi, the country's second biggest bank, has been dismissed after admitting he took bribes in irregular foreign exchange transactions.

- Finance and Economic Planning Minister Aleke Banda urged Blantyre City Council to clear the city's streets of vendors as part of preparations for a September summit of the Southern Africa Development Community.
- Banda also met private road and building contractors to discuss maintenanance issues in preparation for the September summit.

- The opposition Alliance For Democracy party will go ahead with a court case against six members of parliament serving as cabinet ministers in the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) government, legal affairs secretary Bazuka Mhango said.
- The opposition Malawi Congress Party annual convention scheduled for next week has been postponed to mid-July.
